What's new in Vekrun 0.7.7

Honest results
• A run whose tests passed but checked none of what you asked for now says "Not verified" — everywhere: the Work Item, the proof, the Map, Home and the Board. Before, it could read "Passed". Partly verified work says so too, and shows what wasn't checked apart from what failed.
• Not-verified work no longer looks like normal review: no green tick on Proof, and the next step tells you how to get it verified. You can still accept it yourself, with your reason.

Mobile and desktop apps from a prompt
• A new Flutter, Tauri, Electron, Expo, React Native, SwiftUI or Kotlin app now starts instead of stopping with "no test command found". Vekrun checks this Mac's tools (asking once if something must be installed), creates the project with its official starter, and builds from there.
• Planning keeps to a share of the budget, so there's money left to build and test. If its checks can't all be validated in time, the plan is kept — those checks just never count as verified.
• Checks are written in small batches, so long lists of requirements get checks instead of none.
• Work is saved every few minutes during a run. If a build machine disappears, the run carries on in a new one from the last save.
• Proofs say when they ran on a different platform than the app's target, and count skipped tests.
• New: `vekrun factory history <work item> --format ndjson` exports a Work Item's timeline of engineering events in a documented format.

Fewer dead ends
• An expired sign-in pauses the run safely with one "Sign in again" button — or "Run it on <another agent>" when one is signed in. No more silent waits, and no repair attempts wasted on it.
• PHP and Laravel projects get real checks (PHPUnit, Pest, Composer).
• A brand-new project on a stack Vekrun doesn't know gets a test command proposed by its agent (shown in the run log) instead of stopping.
• What you agree before Start — a database, Stripe, email, browser tests — now decides how the build machine is set up.
• Small budgets: the builder keeps back a smaller reserve, and a builder stopped at its limit gets what it built verified, with "Run again" offered.
• Costs show tokens used, and calls on a subscription plan say "no charge reported" instead of $0.00.

Safer Git
• Code in a project can no longer redirect or reconfigure the Git that Vekrun itself runs: Vekrun's Git ignores a repository's fsmonitor, hooks, external diff and textconv programs, and refuses a checkout whose .git points somewhere else. Coding agents can't write .git, and test secrets are written so a planted link can't copy them into your files. Your Git panel keeps your own hooks and settings.
